exact_key_binding.tested_scope: traditional 20-byte Git SHA-1 object IDs only
exact_key_binding.detail: A caller can construct InfoHash directly from the exact 20 bytes or 40 hex digits and pass it to Dht::get without mandatory rehashing. This does not cover SHA-256 Git repositories.

returned_bytes_and_local_git_hash.detail: OpenDHT Value exposes arbitrary payload bytes. Git primary documentation permits local object-ID verification when the verifier has the correct uncompressed '<type> <size>\0' plus object data. The candidate does not establish that any reachable DHT value under the target key contains that canonical representation, so no actual object hash was verified.

passive_preexisting_residency.detail: No primary evidence or observed network response establishes that any target canonical Git object is already resident under its exact Git SHA-1 key. Publishing it first would cease to be passive pre-existing retrieval and would introduce a producer/mutation dependency. Default 10-minute value expiration further weakens any unqualified durability assumption.

scheduled_chat_exposure.detail: OpenDHT source defines an optional HTTP proxy, but the project documentation found here documents running a proxy/node rather than an official public zero-cost proxy endpoint. This scheduled Chat surface has HTTP/repository reads but no native UDP/OpenDHT node interface. Without an already-available public proxy endpoint holding the target value, the route retains an external execution/hosting dependency.

generic_object_coverage.detail: MAX_VALUE_SIZE is 64 KiB. Chunking or an external manifest/mapping could change the architecture, but that is outside the exact direct one-key/one-value scope and is not proven by this candidate.

hidden_executor_check.detail: The optional REST proxy is itself a separately run service; no official pre-existing public proxy endpoint was established in this slice. Treating 'run a node/proxy' as part of the route would be a residual executor/hosted-service step rather than scheduled-Chat-native parity.

verdict.reason: Exact 160-bit key binding is real, but end-to-end passive retrieval is not proven: target residency, actual canonical returned bytes, Chat-exposed zero-dependency access, and generic >64 KiB coverage remain unresolved.
